Q: "Defend" Against Multiple ANSI Styles A:

One idea would be to create a function that filters out the unwanted styles.

library(cli)

sty_1 <- combine_ansi_styles(
  style_italic,
  style_bold,
  style_strikethrough
)

filter_combined_style <- function(x, combined_style, exclude = c()) {
  env <- environment(combined_style)
  all_styles <- env$styles
  
  filtered_styles <- all_styles[!names(all_styles) %in% exclude]
  
  for (style in filtered_styles) {
    x <- paste0(style$open, x, style$close)
  }
  
  structure(x, class = "cli_ansi_string")
}

Then any style that we want to defend against will be added to exclude.

"Example text" |> filter_combined_style(sty_1, 
                                        exclude = c("italic", "strikethrough"))

<cli_ansi_string>

[1]Example text

"Example text" |> filter_combined_style(sty_1, 
                                        exclude = c("italic"))

<cli_ansi_string>

[1]Example text

"Example text" |> filter_combined_style(sty_1)

<cli_ansi_string>

[1]Example text

Q: In Polars, is there a way to replace or modify the lazyframe at the origin of a computation graph? A:

Lazyframe has pipe which seems more like what you want so instead of doing...

step1_lf = base_lf.with_columns(pl.col('a') + 1)

do

def step1(lf):
    return lf.with_columns(pl.col('a') + 1)

and then with any starting lf you can then do lf.pipe(step1)

Q: Rider IDE - 'No projects to run' when trying to run/debug application A:

I had the same issue. In the Project Properties > Web. Ensure the server type is "IIS" and URL to the site is correct. When I clicked OK, it created a run config for IIS automatically.
